text: When the seventh month came and the Israelites were settled in their towns, the people gathered together as one in Jerusalem.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his kinsmen, began to build the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the Law of Moses, the man of God.
Despite their fear of the peoples around them, they set the altar on its old foundation and offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, morning and evening offerings both.
Then they celebrated the Festival of Booths as it is written, sacrificing the number of burnt offerings required for each day, as the rule required.
After that they offered the regular burnt offerings and the offerings for the New Moons and all the appointed sacred festivals of the LORD, as well as those brought as freewill offerings to the LORD.
On the first day of the seventh month they began offering burnt offerings to the LORD, though the foundation of the LORD's temple had not yet been laid.

So they paid the masons and carpenters with silver, and gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre so they would bring cedar logs by sea from Lebanon to Joppa, as authorized by Cyrus king of Persia.

In the second month of the second year after arriving at God's house in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began the work, together with the rest of their people — the priests, the Levites, and all who had returned to Jerusalem from the exile. They appointed the Levites twenty years old and up to oversee the building of the LORD's house.

Jeshua and his sons and brothers, and Kadmiel and his sons, descendants of Judah, joined together to supervise those working on God's house, along with the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers, the Levites.

When the builders laid the foundation of the LORD's temple, the priests in their vestments took their places with trumpets, and the Levites, sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the arrangement of David king of Israel.

With praise and thanksgiving they sang responsively to the LORD: For he is good; his faithful love toward Israel endures forever. And all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD because the foundation of the LORD's house had been laid.
But many of the older priests, Levites, and family heads, who had seen the first temple, wept loudly when they saw the foundation of this house, while many others shouted for joy.
No one could distinguish the sound of the joyful shouting from the sound of the people's weeping, for the people shouted so loudly that the sound was heard far away.
